brief_title: Evaluating the SWW Method Dietary Intervention for HbA1c and Weight Management as a Preventative Intervention in Women
official_title: Evaluating the SWW Method® Dietary Intervention for HbA1c and Weight Management as a Preventative Intervention in Women

interventions.name: SWW Method® Dietary and Lifestyle Intervention

arm_groups.label: Intervention group (cases)
intervention_names: Behavioral: SWW Method® Dietary and Lifestyle Intervention

primary_outcomes.measure: Change in HbA1c Time Frame: Baseline and 12 weeks

brief_summary: This study evaluated the SWW Method®, a 12-week dietary and lifestyle intervention based on the carbohydrate-insulin model, in a healthy cohort of women aged 35-75. The study assessed whether the intervention resulted in significant improvements in blood glucose markers (HbA1c, fasting blood glucose), weight, BMI, and other metabolic markers compared to a no-intervention control group. The SWW Method® protocol includes intermittent fasting, a protein-forward diet, meal sequencing, hydration, magnesium supplementation, and sleep support. This was a non-randomized case-control trial with 45 intervention participants and 40 controls, conducted over 12 weeks.

eligibility.criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Female
* 35-75 years of age
* No prior enrollment in the SWW Method® or Sarah Wragge Wellness® program.

Exclusion Criteria:

* History of non-skin-related cancer diagnosis or treatment within the past five years.
* Currently taking weight loss medication, including semaglutide
* Currently taking any medication for blood sugar or diabetes management.
* Previous enrollment in the SWW Method® or any Sarah Wragge Wellness® program.
